objective: Add provider-neutral fail-closed execution-time intervention admission that binds observed runtime signals to typed bounded controls, target state, recovery checkpoint, policy, generation, expiry, approval, cooldown, post-condition verification, and non-authority boundaries without executing controls.

research_inputs.finding: MCP defines progress, cancellation, and opt-in Tasks for long-running operations with polling, mid-flight input, and durable handles; tool descriptions are untrusted and user consent is required.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL models intervention admission, approval, bounded lifetime, and post-condition evidence without treating MCP metadata or task handles as authority.

research_inputs.finding: Production agent runtimes separate loop ownership, sessions, tracing, guardrails, resumable approval flows, state, handoffs, tools/MCP, and evaluation; runs may pause and resume after approval.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds typed intervention decisions, explicit approval gating, attempt limits, generation fences, and completion receipts separate from execution.

research_inputs.finding: AI Runtime Infrastructure is an execution-time layer that observes long-horizon state and actively intervenes during execution; passive observability and static orchestration are insufficient for runtime failures and safety risks.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds a bounded intervention contract that complements path governance and task lifecycle without embedding models or autonomous privileged self-modification.

features: observation, target state, proposed state, reason, and recovery checkpoint digest binding
one-shot intervention IDs and attempt limits
post-condition state and trace completion receipt
replay/tamper protection and explicit authority boundary

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane receipt overhead; excludes actual process control, model, network, memory, accelerator, and kernel scheduling latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the intervention module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged path-governance release

limitations: The contract emits admission evidence and does not itself pause, checkpoint, downgrade, retry, quarantine, roll back, or terminate any workload.
Observed signals, state digests, checkpoint digests, and approvals are caller-supplied and require independently trusted supervisors and enforcement adapters for production trust.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes real intervention latency, model serving, network, memory, accelerator, and kernel scheduler performance.
The real-task scenarios are deterministic control-plane fixtures and do not establish general intelligence, model quality, browser autonomy, robotics, or production agent efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
